summary: Jersey protects heirs on immovable property (land) with fixed shares, but movables are free. Trusts are well established and foundations are available. The Hague Trusts Convention applies to Jersey.
reserved_share: Heirs have fixed rights over immovable property; a testator with descendants may freely dispose of only part of it (a one-third free portion is often cited); movables are free. Exact figures not confirmed.
foreign_law_note: Movables follow the law of the deceased's domicile, immovables in Jersey follow Jersey law. There is no choice of nationality law.
trust_note: Trusts (Jersey) Law 1984; Hague Convention applies to Jersey (1 March 1992 per the UK Treaty Series correction). Foundations (Jersey) Law 2009 allows private foundations.
open_questions: The HCCH status-table page could be read only in an older cached version that does not show territorial extensions; extension dates come from the UK Treaty Series 14 (1992) and a Dutch treaty record, and should be re-checked on hcch.net.
Exact free portion for Jersey immovables under the Wills and Successions (Jersey) Law 1993.
